newsitem.title: USA: Focus on market share hurts bond insurers -- S&P.
newsitem.headline: Focus on market share hurts bond insurers -- S&P.

text.p: The companies that insure municipal bonds may be focusing too much on market share and not enough on charging prices that maintain appropriate returns, Standard & Poor's Corp said Monday.

In a report in CreditWeek Municipal, S&P said bond insurers guaranteed 51 percent of all municipal bonds that came to market in the third quarter, a rate the agency said reflects an emphasis on defending or building market share.
"As a result of this trend, and in combination with several other factors, current premium rates charged for public finance insurance are generating only adequate returns," the report said.
S&P said corporate history has many examples of industries that pursued market share "much to the detriment of creditors and owners."
The bond insurance industry's average public finance premium for 1995 was about 45 basis points, S&P said. By comparison, average premiums from 1989 through 1992 were about 60 basis points.
"Offsetting the pricing decline to some extent, the mix of business and quality of business -- and associated capital charges -- have improved" during the same period, S&P noted.
S&P also said companies need to take market share into account when considering investor perceptions of the liquidity of insured bonds.

"Since buyers of insured bonds are concerned about the liquidity associated with a bond insurer's paper, they may become concerned and adjust their trading valuations to the extent that they see less insurance written, economic fundamentals for the bond insurer not withstanding," S&P said.
Given those considerations, "the variable that has suffered is premium rates," according to the report.

The top three municipal bond insurers are MBIA Insurance Corp, a unit of MBIA Inc ; AMBAC Indemnity Corp, a unit of AMBAC Inc ; and Financial Guaranty Insurance Co, a unit of GE Capital Services. GE Capital is a subsidiary of General Electric Co.
